_meta.note: 本文件是信息层：只给 Jev 提供决策上下文（usage/doctrine），不改变任何评分或候选生成逻辑。usage_en 按 hybrid_plants.json 的中文名索引。

principles_en: HARD CONSTRAINT (user-confirmed 2026-09-26): the opening Sunflower Queen is MANDATORY - games are very hard to win without her. Save sky-dropped sun toward her while the board is calm (no zombies, or within the opening grace with no critical lane); once zombies are on the lawn past that grace, build minimum defence first and return to the queen when calm. Only cheap (<=150 sun) defensive cards may bypass an active queen save (threatened plant or a zero-defence pressured lane). Once she is down, fill sunflowers behind her.
Economy first: establish 4 producers before buying expensive cards; keep ~300 sun as emergency reserve; never dump all sun at once.
Slow beats burst: a slowed cluster dies to the same DPS many times over; prefer control (slow/stun) plus sustained fire over raw single-target damage.
Every lane needs coverage; zombies pick lanes randomly, one undefended lane loses the game. Keep the hottest lane covered first.

Wall hybrids (nut variants that also shoot) always stand on the FRONT line: their reflect/death effects only work while being bitten. If a wall already exists in the lane, plant them as an extra layer in FRONT of it - never behind it, never in the rear ranks.
Short-range plants (fume-shroom family reach only ~4 cells) must sit at the front edge of the formation, within range of the nearest zombie. Planting them in the rear ranks is a complete waste.

Never idle with full pockets: when the board is quiet, keep building - top up economy, pre-place shooters/walls in lanes that lack them, and keep the formation uniform across lanes. The code offers low-priority prebuild candidates for exactly this.

Emergency layering: when a zombie is within ~2 cells of your front plants, walls may be planted ONTO the zombie's own cell to block instantly. If no wall card is ready on a critical lane, sacrifice a cheap plant (sunflower etc.) on the zombie's cell as a speed bump until the wall card is off cooldown.
Grow the economy column-by-column (fill column A top-to-bottom before column B) so the rear ranks stay tidy and walls/shooters get clean rows.
Walls go on the house side of zombies; shooters stay strictly behind walls; tracking shooters may sit in any safe lane.
Save toward one strong upgrade instead of scattering many cheap plants, unless a lane is urgent.
One-shot bombs are for real emergencies or dense clusters, not single far-away zombies; respect their long cooldowns.
enemy_notes_en: Normal zombie: 270 hp, bites 100/s, slow. Any shooter handles it.

Armored zombies (e.g. bucket: ~1100+270, armor class 1; screen doors: class 2): plain peas are inefficient. Prefer armor-breaking damage (thunder plant hits armor double), butter stun (cattail hybrids), or charm (note: 2nd-class armor absorbs one charm hit).

Giant-type zombies (gargantua/ice-truck): smash around 1800, most walls die in one hit. Only crush-resistant walls (tall nut variants resisting 8 hits) or cheat-death walls (lose 800, reflect 800) hold them; butter stun and charm buy time (ice-truck vehicle takes 1800 instead of being charmed).
Jumping zombies: they leap over normal walls; the reclaimable tall nut blocks jumps.
Ice-trail zombies: they leave ice that slows the lane; the cherry-chili burst destroys ice trails and cancels ice slow.
Control-immune helmets: charm does not work on them; use damage instead.
Zombie identities are unverified at runtime; reason from observed body_hp, armor_hp and x position, not from guessed names.

RANGED ZOMBIES (zombie peashooter family) stand still and shoot: they kill uncovered expensive plants across the lawn, and a whole row of shooters can be wiped in the pool. Keep a wall in front of EVERY expensive (300+ sun) shooter; the code detects stationary zombies automatically and boosts wall candidates on their lanes.

CRUSHING ZOMBIES (ice-truck / newspaper-truck fusions) squash normal plants outright instead of chewing. CORRECTION (user 2026-09-26): Ice Wall-nut does NOT resist crushing - only 雷果子 and 高冰果 do (the truck pops its tire the moment it hits them), so when the push cannot be stopped otherwise, those two are the blockers to throw at it. Cells the truck has driven over are SNOW-COVERED and cannot be planted until the snow melts - a failed placement there is the game refusing, not a bug. Prefer crush-resistant walls on those lanes and spend ash bursts early.

SALVAGE TECHNIQUE (user-confirmed): shoveling a plant in this build REFUNDS SUN. A nearly-dead plant (about to be chewed through within one decision cycle) or a non-crush-resistant plant about to be squashed should be shoveled immediately - sun beats a wasted plant. 雷果子/高冰果 are never salvage-shoveled for crushing (they survive it).
BLACK FOOTBALL-type zombies eat AND move faster than normal zombies (bite ~150/s vs 100/s). Judge timing per zombie type, not by the average pace.

SUN BOMB geometry: the blast is a 3x3 grid (nine cells) around the target cell. Prefer placements that catch the MOST zombies in that grid - every kill refunds sun - but never wait for a full grid when the situation is urgent.

TORCH COLUMN SPACING: never plant Sunflower Queens in the same row - each one is a torch column, spread them across lanes. Torch-compatible shooters (Wild Gatling first, Corn Cattail second, Peashooter last) should sit BEHIND a queen to pass through fire for bonus damage. Mid-late game, if a cheap sunflower/peashooter occupies the golden cell right behind a queen and sun is ample, shovel it (refunds sun) and upgrade to a torch-boosted heavy hitter.

usage_en.向日葵女王: First costs 500 sun; add 100 for each same-type plant currently on the field. Prefer column C (third column), with torch-compatible peas behind in A/B. Produces 150 sun per 25s and 80 nominal tracking DPS; when this covers weak enemies, keep growing the economy. Do not classify every ordinary zombie as an emergency.
usage_en.阳光向日葵: Base economy. Cheap and grows at 120s (40 -> 75 sun/25s). Plant column-by-column in the safest rear columns (fill column A before column B); with 400 opening sun, a few of these - or saving up for the Sunflower Queen - are both valid opens.
usage_en.冰瓜香蒲: Strongest sustained control: full-board homing melons, every hit slows, 40% deep-freeze. 300 hp only - any safe rear lane works since it tracks the whole board. Best answer when many lanes are pressured or against fast/clustering zombies.
usage_en.狂野机枪射手: Highest single-lane burst (theoretical 200/s; ~half realistic due to 5-angle spread). Lane-locked: put it behind a wall in the single most pressured lane, ideally paired with slow support. Wrong tool for cross-lane problems.
usage_en.玉米卷香蒲: Full-board tracking (20+40)x2 with chance of butter stun that locks even giants. Place in any safe rear lane; great utility when lanes have armored or giant threats that need interrupting.
usage_en.阳光炸弹: 1800 burst in a 1.5-cell circle; destroyed zombies convert to sun. Spend on dense weak-zombie clusters to fight and profit at once; poor against single heavy armor; 50s cooldown - worth more with 3+ zombies in the circle.
usage_en.樱桃辣椒: 1800 damage across 3 full rows and the only answer here that destroys ice trails and cancels ice slow. Long 100s cooldown: keep it for 3-lane pushes or ice-trail emergencies, not single-lane cleanups.
usage_en.雪花寒冰菇: 4000 hp; 8s ice rain (20/s to every zombie) then a 3s full-board freeze plus 15s slow. Board-wide panic button for big waves; freeze is delayed (after the rain), so use it to buy time, not to instantly save a collapsed lane.
usage_en.寒光菇: One-shot full-board Ice-shroom effect, pays 15 sun per frozen zombie. Economy-control: use on crowded boards (6+ zombies) so the freeze also refunds sun; immune/already-frozen targets may pay nothing.
usage_en.回收高坚果: Reusable 8000 hp wall, anti-jump. Prefer column E or farther forward; emergency placement can be closer to the house. Once safe, relocate rear walls: prepare destination Lily Pad if needed, use shovel key 1, verify removal, pick the actual dropped card, verify held seed, then plant and verify destination. Each shovel costs 800 hp; never reclaim at 800 hp or less. A disappeared wall is not yet a successfully recovered/replanted wall.
usage_en.高冰果: Elite wall: 8000 hp, shoots 20x8/1.5s with slow, reflects and may freeze biters, resists 8 crush/hammer hits (1001 each), and releases an Ice-shroom effect on death. +100 price per extra copy. FRONT line only - giant/ice-truck lanes or the hottest lane; if a wall already exists, add it as a layer in FRONT of that wall; put full-range shooters behind.
usage_en.雷果子: Wall+shooter: fires a LASER that rakes the whole lane (60/1.5s, double vs armor), 25% stun, reflects 80/s while bitten, cannot die - a lethal hit costs it 800 hp and reflects 800. +100 price per extra copy. FRONT line only: add in front of an existing wall, never behind; the laser covers the lane from there.
usage_en.冰冻坚果: Budget wall+shooter: shoots 20x2 slowing bullets, reflects 20/s against biters, and freezes its 3x3 for 3s (plus 20s slow) on death. Cheap (150 sun) FRONT-line wall for any lane; place it where it will actually be bitten so its death freeze hits the push. Almanac does not show its hp - assume it dies faster than tall-nut walls.
usage_en.Cupid魅惑菇射手: Temporary (15s): charms ~3 zombies per 2s, flipping them to fight for you; 2nd-class armor absorbs one hit and the ice-truck giant's vehicle takes 1800 instead; control-immune helmets are unaffected. Use as a mid-lane trump card behind a wall against heavy mixed pushes; plan the defence that takes over when she expires.
usage_en.睡莲: Peashooter Lily Pad: water support layer plus modest lane pea fire. An ordinary top-layer plant can coexist. Peas may benefit from a torch in their path. Exact firing numbers are unverified. Complete a planned affordable ready follow-up immediately at the same cell after verifying the pad; its modest shooting does not make a bare pad sufficient defence against heavy pushes.
